risk.title: Risk-Based Access Engine
risk.subtitle: Every access request is scored over eight components - user, device, asset, time, location, behavior, ticket and command - each read from a measured input (the subject's own 24h history, the discovered inventory, the live command policy, the local clock, the source address, the ticket's shape). risk.enforcementBody: Session starts run this same scorer with the operator's device and target: a CRITICAL band refuses the start outright, HIGH proceeds only under an active JIT grant (signed off by someone other than the requester), MEDIUM prescribes MFA, LOW allows. Console evaluations only advise - every evaluation, allowed or refused, is written to the risk trail of the immutable audit ledger.

anomalies.title: Anomalies
anomalies.subtitle: Baselines are learned from this platform's own history - recorded evaluations, sessions, commands and incidents over a rolling window, never synthetic users - and describe how each principal actually works: their hours, devices, source IPs, targets, command verbs and privilege verbs. Every request from a trained principal is diffed against that profile; the deviations are named on the behavior component (5 points each). A CRITICAL deviation refuses the session start, ends the principal's standing sessions through the release-and-rotate cascade, rotates the credential the request sought through the real rotation pipeline, and records the incident below and on the risk trail of the audit ledger.

rail.actorHint: Recorded verbatim as X-Actor on every action (currently {{actor}}). The server enforces dual approval: the requester cannot approve their own emergency and a second signature must come from someone else.
rail.step1: 1. File — an operator states the target, severity, protocol and reason.
rail.step2: 2. First signature — an approver who is not the requester signs (1/2). Nothing is released yet.
rail.step3: 3. Second signature — a different approver signs (2/2) → status approved.
rail.step4: 4. Unseal — the emergency credential is released through the real vault checkout; the recorded session starts.
rail.step5: 5. Close — the session ends, the credential is rotated and the review note is filed.
rail.safeguard1: Recording forced — the emergency session is always recorded.
rail.safeguard2: Real vault checkout — the credential is never shown, only checked out.
rail.safeguard3: Rotation guaranteed — closing the emergency rotates the credential.
rail.safeguard4: Audited end to end — every step lands in the immutable ledger under source break-glass.
rail.safeguard5: Review required — the server refuses to close an emergency without a review note.
